newsitem.title: FRANCE: French fishermen suspend Channel blockade.
newsitem.headline: French fishermen suspend Channel blockade.

text.p: Striking fishermen suspended a blockade of French Channel ports on Thursday as they met French Agriculture Minister Philipe Vasseur to try to settle a dispute over European Union regulations, a port spokesman said.
He said the blockade, which began on Tuesday and has stranded hundreds of trucks on both sides of the Channel, had been lifted at Boulogne, Calais and Dunkirk.
The spokesman for the Boulogne port authority said the protesters had warned they may resume the blockade later in the day depending on the outcome of their talks with the minister.
A French court had ordered the fishermen on Wednesday to lift the blockade, granting an injunction to European ferry giants P&O, Stena Line AB and Sea France.
The spokesman said the ferry Picasso, which had been unable to enter the Boulogne port overnight, moored just after the blockade was lifted and was preparing to cross back to Britain.

A spokeswoman for the Ministry of Agriculture and Fisheries said the fishermen had arrived late for the talks and were discussing their protest over EU regulations calling for larger holes in the mesh of the nets.
The fishermen say larger holes may cut their catch by half.
The blockade by fishing boats, as France embarks on a campaign for an early parliamentary election next month, has crippled traffic to and from the three ports.

Hundreds of trucks were backed up on a motorway near the British port of Dover because of the blockade while thousands of travellers faced delays as ferries were diverted to the Belgian ports of Zeebrugge and Ostend.
